chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ayyar and Hammad ibn Isa, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who threw the Jamarat (pillars) in a disordered manner: He said, 'He must repeat for the Middle one and the Jamarat al-Aqaba.' If he had thrown from the first Jamarah less than four pebbles and completed the last two Jamarat, he must repeat for all three Jamarat. And if he had thrown four from the first, he should complete that and not repeat for the last two. And likewise, if he had thrown three from the second, he must repeat for it and for the third. And if he had thrown four for both of them and thrown seven for the third, he should complete them and not repeat for the third. Narrated.

key_terms.رَمَى الْجِمَارَ: Threw pebbles at the Jamarat pillars
key_terms.مَنْكُوسَةً: In a disordered or reversed manner

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim throws the Jamarat pebbles out of order during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* outlines the precise fiqh of *mankusah* (throwing out of order) during the stoning of the Jamarat, emphasizing the Shia scholarly focus on the validity of the sequence (*tartib*) as a condition for the ritual's completeness. It provides a detailed algorithmic approach to rectification, distinguishing between partial completion and full repetition based on the number of pebbles cast at each pillar, reflecting the rigorous legal methodology of the Imams. This ruling underscores the importance of intentionality and order in Hajj rituals, ensuring the pilgrim fulfills the Sunnah accurately.
